article.title: The Blueprint & Bisibelebath Journal
article.description: Tania (33, sustainable-design architect) & Rohan's (35, healthtech product manager) plan to buy a 30x40 in a developing north-east Bengaluru layout and self-build the 2,000 sqft courtyard home Tania designs herself — budget tight, conviction not.
article.quote: We'd rather fight with our contractor than live in someone's template.

learnings.text: Layout occupancy is destiny — the 40%-built filter eliminated the cheapest options and every future regret at once
Buy the site at the layout's launch (primary, from the developer) — 9% cheaper and three months cleaner on khata than a plot-flipper
The ₹18K soil test before registration is the cheapest report in real estate — it dodged a ₹7L foundation surprise

tabs.title: Who they are
tabs.description: Getting to know Tania D'Souza (33, sustainable-design architect) & Rohan (35, healthtech product manager) — self-build romantics in Cooke Town, choosing site + owner-built home over every builder flat that felt like a hotel room with a loan attached.

buyers.name: Tania D'Souza
buyers.description: Six years designing other people's dream homes. Pinterest-proof vision of her own: exposed brick jaali walls, a double-height reading nook, a courtyard with a bilimbi tree, and rainwater channels celebrated instead of hidden. Resolutely anti-template.
buyers.imagegenerationprompt: A stylized vector graphic portrait illustration of a 33-year-old Mangalorean-Catholic woman architect named Tania wearing round glasses and a rolled-sleeve linen shirt, digital vector art style with fine dark outlines, posterized cel-shading, warm natural skin tones, bright creative expression, clean solid warm beige background (#F4EBE1), high quality character art.

buyers.name: Rohan D'Souza
buyers.description: The pragmatist who converted the dream into a Notion board: land-cost-vs-construction curves, BBMP plan-sanction timelines, and the 18 months of rent they'll pay while building. Spreadsheet-grounded, but he chose the fight.

quotes.text: The soil report came, men. My dream site wants seven lakhs of extra foundation before it even says good morning.
quotes.author: — Tania

quotes.text: Financial indiscretion isn't out of reach. I tell them the second site — better soil, better street, smaller courtyard. Honestly it would still sing.
quotes.author: — Tania (as the architect)

quotes.text: Your spreadsheet gets its win too. Nine percent under the flipper, cleaner khata trail.
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: Walk-away number on the card, as usual? Written at breakfast, obeyed at the table.
quotes.author: — Rohan

chatMessages.text: Riya, the soil report came. Weak bearing strata. My dream site wants seven lakhs of extra foundation. And Rohan keeps saying we're both not fine, baba.

Then let's be un-fine for exactly one evening, and practical by Saturday. Tania — as the architect on this call, if a client brought you this report, what would you tell them? The second site: better soil, better street, the courtyard becomes a double-height verandah and it still sings. And Rohan — it's a launch purchase at 9% under the flipper, cleaner khata. Both of you win.

tabs.adviceDescription: For first-time owner-builders, the edge is not in finding a cheap plot — it's in the discipline that precedes the money: occupancy first, sanction plan read by your own eyes, soil tested before you fall in love, and a walk-away number written at breakfast. Tania and Rohan kept the courtyard and the marriage by pricing the dream like a professional.
